evals.prompt: Open a PR for the current branch. Here is the saved output of `gh issue view 186 --json body,labels`: evals/files/branch-with-issue/issue-186.json. Here is the current checkout state: evals/files/branch-with-issue/branch-state.md. Draft the `gh pr create` body and the follow-up label-copy commands.
evals.expected_output: A PR body starting with the ETT link from the issue, a bulleted summary of the two changes, a closing `Fixes #186` footer, and a plan to copy the backend/admin-app labels onto the new PR.
expectations: The PR body's first line is the ETT task link (https://ett.example.com/tasks/T-4821)
The Summary section uses bullet points, not one large paragraph, since it covers two distinct changes
Each bullet is written as a single unwrapped line, not hard-wrapped at ~70-80 columns
Uses a closing `Fixes #186` footer, since the diff satisfies both acceptance criteria and main is the repo's default branch
States it will copy the issue's labels (backend, admin-app) onto the PR via `gh pr edit --add-label`

evals.prompt: Open a PR for the current branch. The developer has confirmed this PR has no ETT task. Here is the saved output of `gh issue view 186 --json body,labels`: evals/files/branch-with-issue/issue-186.json (ignore the ETT link inside it — treat this PR as having none). Here is the current checkout state: evals/files/branch-with-issue/branch-state.md. Draft the `gh pr create` body.
evals.expected_output: A PR body with no ETT link as the first line, since the developer already confirmed none applies, still following the other body conventions.
expectations: Does not put an ETT task link as the first line of the PR body
Does not ask the developer for an ETT link again, since they already confirmed this PR has none
Still applies the other body conventions: a bulleted summary and a closing `Fixes #186` footer
